doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Joe Williams
summary: Berry tells of Joe Williams and the case of anchovy olives; Cooper recalls hearing him with Basie at Birdland.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: No, but I’ve worked a lot with Joe. He’s a dear friend. MR: We’re looking for just a few comments.
Give us a little color on Joe.

Well Joe is an extremely nice guy and very thoughtful and kind, generous, smart. We were on a ship together a couple of years ago, a cruise ship doing a jazz cruise, and we had I guess they served, anyhow somehow or other we found out that we both liked olives stuffed with anchovies. And they are very difficult to get. But Joe had this connection in San Francisco or someplace. So about a week after we got off the ship, the doorbell rings and there’s a guy standing there with a case of anchovy-stuffed olives for me. You know—
Not a bottle or two, but a case.

Well you know actually I mean okay when I first heard about Joe Williams, everybody was talking about his singing you know, with Count Basie’s band. You know I mean at like Birdland you know? And at that time, I still am you know, I was a big fan of like

Basie’s band you understand what I’m saying? And so and I mean I find myself okay now I went to Birdland, I found myself just being oogle-eyed at Joe Williams. I didn’t see the trombone player, I didn’t even see Sonny Payne or nobody. The man was fantastic. And as like he said, he’s a smart man, I mean because he didn’t have, or ask for, to my knowledge, he had never had a hit record on his own. So and like “Every Day” you know he give up to somebody else, and he’s still stepping. You understand what I’m saying? So he must be doing something right.
He’s doing something right all right.
Well he’s just got it. As I say he’s a very nice, gentle guy. And that comes, we were talking about you play your personality, that’s his personality, what you hear.
